invariants: Military occupation is not sovereignty by itself.
Treaties require persisted consent from every party before becoming active.
Bounties cannot pay more currency than was escrowed.
Settlement founding transfers existing people; it never creates population.
Recruitment rights are a governance fact separate from population and force ownership.
Governance tax policy only moves conserved money from real taxable economic activity into the exact jurisdiction treasury; tax policy never mints scheduled population income.
Active military-access agreements authorize only the exact grantee, governed place set, and optional route set recorded in typed provisions.
Tribute settlement transfers the typed amount between real funding holders and cannot mint currency.

Founded settlement civil-economy reviews derive aggregate workforce, activity, consumption, service/food pressure, and attractiveness from conserved resident pools; fiscal settlement moves only currency already present in a real regional private-economy holder.
Nonaggression, alliance, ceasefire, guarantee, and client-state relations constrain state-level hostile conflict initiation according to their typed scope.
Alliance, guarantee, and client-state defense duties triggered by an attack become exact timed obligation commitments rather than narrative-only promises.

Active trade agreements modify real route tax settlement through typed tariff multipliers; border agreements constrain exact strategic crossing routes; client-state patronage grants the patron strategic access to the client jurisdiction.
